identity.name: Mauro-Roman Kingdom
alt_names: Kingdom of the Moors and Romans

land.text: much of Mauretania Caesariensis around Altava: 'Military independence from the Western Roman Empire: 429'

predecessors.note: The Vandals took the rest of Roman Africa from 435 (Aures page); the Mauro-Roman page gives no founding date for the kingdom or for Masuna's rule.

land.text: the rump state at Altava after Garmul's defeat and death in 578

successors.note: The Mauro-Roman page also names the Kingdom of Ouarsenis and the Kingdom of Hodna among its regional successors, without dates; the infobox puts the decline at 599, the text 'roughly 589-599'.

capitals.name: Altava (Ouled Mimoun)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Altava'; a fortification inscription at Altava dated 508 AD styles Masuna 'rex gentium Maurorum et Romanorum'. Coordinates approximate (not in the gazetteer).

correction.text: 'much of Mauretania Caesariensis' ruled from Altava

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page says the kingdom 'dominated much of Mauretania Caesariensis from Altava', gives no area and no frontier, and does not date the kingdom's growth; the Oranais region plus a 150 km circle around Algiers is the researcher's reading of Mauretania Caesariensis, as in the Altava dossier.

ledger.note: 429: the Moors of Mauretania Caesariensis gain military independence from the Western Roman Empire (infobox 'Military independence from the Western Roman Empire: 429'). The page gives no founding date for the kingdom itself; Masuna's inscription at Altava is of 508 and the ruler list starts c. 477.

region.text: the Mauro-Roman Kingdom, left to the rump state of Altava and the regional kingdoms

ledger.note: 578: Garmul is defeated and killed and the kingdom shrinks to Altava. 'Generals Theodore and Theoctistus were killed in 570 AD, and Amabilis in 571 AD. The campaign against him ran 577-78 AD, and the text says he was defeated and killed in 578 AD.' The Altava page: 'Collapse of the Mauro-Roman Kingdom: 578'.

wars.name: Massonas and the Eastern Romans against the Vandals
wars.outcome: 'Massonas allied with the Eastern Romans against the Vandals in 535 AD, according to Procopius.'

wars.name: Garmul's war on the Eastern Romans
wars.outcome: Garmul raided from the late 560s; generals Theodore and Theoctistus were killed in 570 and Amabilis in 571; the campaign against him ran 577-78 and he was killed in 578, after which the kingdom shrank to Altava.

certainty.note: A Moorish-Roman kingdom of the Algerian highlands: no page gives a frontier.

notes: Cliopatria has no Mauro-Roman row. Pages disagree on the end: the Mauro-Roman page's infobox gives the decline at 599 and its text 'until roughly 589-599', the Altava page gives the collapse as 578 and Garmul's reign c. 570-579; 578 (Garmul's death) is used and the 579-599 remnant is the Altava dossier. The Mauro-Roman page gives no founding date; 429 is the infobox's military independence, and the Aures page gives the same 429 for its own separation, so the two states' beginnings are not distinguished on the pages. The infobox rulers (Mephanias? c. 477, Masuna c. 508, Mastigas c. 541, Stotzas 541-545, John 545-546, Garmul c. 570-579) mix Moorish kings with Byzantine officers and are not entered as a ruler strip. The Vandal wars of Gunthamund and Thrasamund (and Cabaon's victory over a Vandal army) are undated on the page and are not entered as a war. The Kingdoms of Ouarsenis and Hodna (regional successors) and the Aures kingdom (separate dossier kingdom-of-the-aures) are neighbours; the Mauretania Caesariensis extent is the researcher's reading and overlaps the Vandal Kingdom row of Cliopatria west of 3 E only at the margin. Gazetteer: Oranais and Algiers resolve; Altava is not a gazetteer place.
